did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel sees above the heads of the cherubim a vault resembling sapphire, and above it the appearance of a throne.
Did you know? The man dressed in linen is commanded to take coals of fire from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.
Did you know? The sound of the cherubim’s wings is heard as far as the outer court and is described as the voice of God Almighty speaking.
Did you know? In this chapter, one of the cherubim reaches out his hand to the fire among the cherubim and places it into the hands of the man dressed in linen.
Did you know? Under their wings, the cherubim appear to have something resembling human hands.
Did you know? Ezekiel describes four wheels, one beside each cherub, whose appearance is like that of a precious stone.
Did you know? The four wheels are alike, and their description includes the image of a wheel within a wheel.
Did you know? The wheels are described as being full of eyes all around, as are the bodies, backs, hands, and wings of the cherubim.
Did you know? Ezekiel hears the wheels being called “the whirling wheels.”

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, Ezekiel identifies the living creatures he saw by the river as the cherubim, describing each one as having four faces, four wings, and hands resembling human hands.
